single_mapping_proof: scripts/quant/tests/test_f1r_b_production_recording_integration.py:test_03_there_is_exactly_one_version_mapping scans every module under src/w2 and scripts/quant and asserts no declared version string appears outside the authority module.
why_not_the_factor_registry: config/factors/factor_registry.v1.json carries a governance version used for lifecycle decisions (ACTIVE, SCORING, numeric_effect_enabled). It is 1 for every factor and does not change when an algorithm changes, so it cannot identify the computation that produced a score.
why_not_a_commit_or_deploy_sha: A commit SHA changes on every unrelated edit and does not change when only a builder's behaviour changes through a dependency. It identifies a tree, not a computation.
binding_rules: The version is read from the authority, never supplied by the caller.
A caller must declare the version it believes it ran; a declaration that differs from the authority refuses the whole batch with FACTOR_VERSION_DISAGREES_WITH_BUILDER_AUTHORITY.
A missing or blank declaration refuses the whole batch with FACTOR_VERSION_MISSING.
An undeclared factor refuses with FACTOR_COMPUTATION_VERSION_UNKNOWN; there is no default.
factor_version is one of the seventeen protected fields, so changing a version changes factor_input_hash, factor_verdict_hash and observation_id.

algorithm_pin.what: Each declaration pins the SHA-256 of its builder function's own source text and the reason code that builder emits when it computes.
algorithm_pin.why: A version that does not move when the algorithm moves is worthless. The pin is per function, not per file, so changing one factor does not force a spurious bump on the others that share a module.
algorithm_pin.enforced_by: scripts/quant/tests/test_f1r_b_production_recording_integration.py:test_03_the_version_authority_matches_the_executed_builder, which imports the builder, hashes inspect.getsource(builder) and asserts the reason code appears in that source.
algorithm_pin.on_change: Editing a builder fails the lock test until its version is revised. Revising the version changes every subsequent observation identity, which is the intended consequence.

F5_RECENT_AH_COVER.note: The version is bound even though F5 cannot currently participate. A version that only appeared once a factor scored would be missing from exactly the records that document why it did not.

builder_files_unmodified.statement: F1R-B did not modify src/w2/features/team_factors.py or src/w2/features/live_factors.py.
builder_files_unmodified.why_it_matters: The frozen F1 package pins both files' SHA-256 in F1_SOURCE_INVENTORY.jsonl as its SOURCE_CODE_DEFAULT weight evidence, and regenerating that package compares the live files against those hashes. Declaring the versions in a separate domain module rather than inside the builders keeps that freeze intact.

known_limitation.what: The version is declared beside the builder rather than emitted by it. A contribution object does not carry its own factor_version.
known_limitation.consequence: The caller/builder disagreement check compares the caller's declaration against the authority, not against a value the builder returned at runtime.
known_limitation.why: Emitting it would require adding a field to FeatureContribution and setting it in both builder modules, which changes the two files the frozen F1 package pins. The algorithm pin above is the compensating control: the authority cannot drift from the builder without failing a test.
known_limitation.how_to_close: If a future task is authorised to re-freeze F1's source inventory, add factor_version to FeatureContribution, set it from this authority in every builder branch, and tighten the check to compare all three values.
